title: META Stock Jumps To Two-Month High — Muse Seen As A 'Notable' Revenue Stream By TD Cowen, While Meta Reportedly Buys A Swedish AI Startup
detail:
META Stock Jumps To Two-Month High — Muse Seen As A 'Notable' Revenue Stream By TD Cowen, While Meta Reportedly Buys A Swedish AI Startup
META Stock Jumps To Two-Month High — Muse Seen As A 'Notable' Revenue Stream By TD Cowen, While Meta Reportedly Buys A Swedish AI Startup · Stocktwits
Shashank Nayar
Wed, September 9, 2026 at 1:15 PM CDT 3 min read
META
SHOP
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

TD Cowen is maintaining a Buy rating and $750 price target on Meta shares and sees Meta Muse AI as a notable revenue stream.

Meta has acquired Stockholm-based AI startup Stilla.ai to integrate its technology and team into the Meta Business Agent ecosystem.

Tech leaders including Shopify CEO Tobi Lütke and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan praised Meta Muse rollout.

Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) stock jumped about 6% on Wednesday to its best in two months after analysts at TD Cowen recognized Meta Muse AI to be a 'notable' revenue stream in the future, while reports suggested Meta acquired a Swedish AI firm to bolster its business AI agents.

TD Cowen said the firm is not modeling near-term revenue from Muse, but thinks the offering "could evolve into a notable [revenue] stream over the longer term." TD keeps a Buy rating and $750 price target on Meta shares, a near 22% upside from Tuesday's closing price.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Meta continues to navigate investor concern over its aggressive capital expenditure, which was raised to a range of $125 billion to $145 billion for 2026. While Meta's shares have faced pressure year-to-date, down about 0.8%, the company's continuous investments in underlying infrastructure and personal assistant ecosystems are seen as foundation-building for long-term monetization.

Strategic Acquisition Of Swedish AI Startup Stilla.ai

Complementing the release of Muse, Meta has acquired Stockholm-based artificial intelligence startup Stilla.ai. Founded in 2024, Stilla.ai raised $5 million earlier this year upon emerging from stealth mode.

Under the transaction, Stilla.ai's team and core technology will be integrated directly into Meta. The acquisition is structured to accelerate the growth of the Meta Business Agent initiative, enhancing automated commerce and transaction handling across WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger.

Meta's 'Muse' Personal AI Agent

Meta officially launched Muse on Tuesday, an autonomous personal AI assistant powered by the Muse Spark 1.3 foundation model. Designed by Meta Superintelligence Labs (MSL) and led on the engineering front by former Stripe CTO David Singleton, the tool represents a shift from traditional conversational chatbots to active digital agents that complete complex, multi-step real-world tasks.

Operating continuously via individual cloud-hosted virtual computers, Muse handles everyday administrative responsibilities including scheduling appointments, buying products, reserving tickets, and filling out electronic forms.

title: Why Meta Platforms Stock Rallied Today
detail:
Why Meta Platforms Stock Rallied Today
Danny Vena, CPA, The Motley Fool
Wed, September 9, 2026 at 11:32 AM CDT 3 min read
META
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Shares of Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) rallied Wednesday morning, gaining as much as 7.2%. As of 12:05 p.m. ET, the stock was still up 6.5%.

The catalyst that sent the social media and artificial intelligence (AI) specialist higher was the launch of an AI agent for the masses.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.
A new way to make money

In a blog post published late on Tuesday, Meta introduced Muse, which the company describes as "the world's first personal AI agent built for everyone." The capabilities of Muse go beyond those of simple chatbots, allowing the agent to complete more complex tasks. Users can communicate with Muse using simple commands, instructing the agent to send emails, schedule appointments, make online purchases, or book dinner reservations.

Muse is connected to Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, giving the agent insight into the user. It can also be linked to a host of third-party apps, including OpenTable, Ticketmaster, Spotify, and Shopify, among others.

Meta will offer both free and paid versions of the agent. The free version will limit usage, but those wanting more can upgrade to either the $20 or $100 tier, depending on usage. Muse will be available to users 18 years and older in the U.S. and can be downloaded from multiple app stores, via WhatsApp, or at the muse.ai website beginning on Tuesday. Later this year, the company will introduce the Muse Confidential Virtual Machine (VM), which will encrypt data accessible only to the user. The company ensures "Not even Meta can access it."

Investors are betting that this will mark a new profit center for Meta. More than 3.6 billion people accessed one of the company's platforms in June, giving Meta a massive target market. If only a small percentage of the company's overall user base subscribes to Muse, the company could generate a notable increase in its revenue.

Even after today's rally, Meta is selling for less than 25 times earnings, an attractive price for a company with so many ways to win.
